episode_policy: Each episode is a self-contained story and advances the series arc. Research and fact-check every factual claim before scripting. Film only genuine original camera recordings with retained source files and verified rights. Never substitute stock footage, AI-generated video, staged encounters or animation.
production_status: PLANNED — no episode is production-ready until genuine original camera footage, rights, factual review and final human approval are recorded.

episodes.topic: How crocodiles use patience, positioning and their environment when ambushing prey.
episodes.hook: The river looks empty — until the surface moves.
story_beats: Open on a real, unaltered observation of a crocodile in its habitat
Explain the documented behaviour and environmental context
Show how patience and positioning fit the animal's hunting strategy
Separate observed footage from researched explanation
Close by introducing the sensory world beneath the surface
episodes.next_episode_teaser: Next: how a crocodile detects and responds to a world beneath the water.

episodes.topic: Crocodile sensory adaptations and how they perceive movement and their surroundings.
episodes.hook: Under the surface, a crocodile is responding to details we can barely see.
story_beats: Begin with an authentic underwater or waterline observation
Explain sensory structures only after checking authoritative research
Connect each explanation to visible behaviour without overstating what the camera proves
Clarify the difference between established science and inference
Tease the mechanics of the ambush
episodes.next_episode_teaser: Next: the mechanics of the strike — and why the waiting matters.

episodes.topic: The sequence, mechanics and ecological context of crocodile hunting behaviour.
episodes.hook: The strike is fast. The waiting is the real story.
story_beats: Start with genuine footage that shows the behaviour without misleading edits
Establish the sequence before explaining it
Use sourced research for bite, movement and hunting claims
Avoid graphic close-ups and sensational claims
Connect hunting behaviour to the animal's habitat
episodes.next_episode_teaser: Next: the hidden story of nests, hatchlings and early survival.

episodes.topic: Nesting, hatchlings, early survival and documented parental behaviour.
episodes.hook: For an animal this powerful, life begins in a surprisingly vulnerable place.
story_beats: Open with naturally recorded nesting or hatchling footage only if available
Verify species-specific nesting and parental-care facts
Explain threats to eggs and hatchlings using reliable sources
Avoid disturbing nests or approaching vulnerable animals
Bridge to seasonal habitat pressures
episodes.next_episode_teaser: Next: what happens when changing water levels reshape a crocodile's habitat.

episodes.topic: Seasonal water levels, habitat change, competition and survival pressures.
episodes.hook: When the water changes, the whole habitat changes with it.
story_beats: Show a real, location-identified habitat observation
Use local ecological sources for seasonal and hydrological context
Distinguish species-wide facts from local observations
Explain how habitat conditions affect wildlife without implying a universal pattern
Set up the wider ecological role of crocodiles
episodes.next_episode_teaser: Final episode: what crocodiles reveal about the health of the river ecosystem.

episodes.topic: Crocodiles in the wider ecosystem, coexistence and conservation context.
episodes.hook: A crocodile's story reaches far beyond the animal itself.
story_beats: Open with a wide, authentic habitat sequence
Explain ecological relationships using authoritative sources
Include conservation context only where location and species evidence support it
Avoid simplistic claims that one species alone controls ecosystem health
Resolve the series arc and invite viewers to continue with the next Wild Encounters series
episodes.next_episode_teaser: The next Wild Encounters series follows another species through its real habitat and behaviour.
